title: Laocoön contributor and utility scores, profiles, uncapped tiers

focus.title: People / + threads / + topics — 81, 387, 427 nodes
focus.ask: The cap is gone and topics are a tier, so the space is walkable: click a topic to see its threads, a thread to see who is in it, a person to see their record. Is the topic tier what you needed to reason about the space, or does it need to carry something else?

focus.title: Contributor score is now an S-curve
focus.ask: 0 units scores 0, 3 units 12, 8 units 41, 12 units 66, 20 units 92. Steepest where the interesting distinctions are, flat at the top so 83 RFCs and 25 land together. Weights are 1 per RFC, 1 per adopted draft, 5 for chairing now, 2 for having chaired, 4 for AD/IAB/IESG. Are those the right weights?

focus.title: Utility score: 36 high, 156 medium, 198 low
focus.ask: Low is either a thread of 6+ that two or three accounts carried at 80%+, or a short exchange between two accounts with no published record. Two experts working a detail score the same as two amplifying accounts — there is a test asserting that, because the day they differ is the day this became a provenance detector. Is that the right line?
